Messages.Author: Jack Vinson
Messages.Body:
>>>>> "b" == babs <ila...@netcom.com> writes:

b> when a vampire gets out of torpor, back to being ready, does he get to
b> hunt in the same turn if she has no blood on her? or does she need to
b> wait for the next turn?

As long as the vampire was untapped in torpor, they MAY hunt. Vampires
untap in torpor as normal, unless they are paralyzed.

The rules indicate that if a ready vampire begins the minion phase without
blood, it must hunt as the first action of the minion phase. However,
torporized vampires are not "ready" and may be able to take other actions
once they are revived. However, it is not terribly advisable for them to
do this.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
ila...@netcom.com (babs) writes:

>when a vampire gets out of torpor, back to being ready, does he get to
>hunt in the same turn if she has no blood on her? or does she need to
>wait for the next turn?

If she is untapped (with no blood) she *must* hunt. This hunt must
be the next minion action you take.
If she is tapped she cannot hunt.

Vamps in torpor untap during the untap phase just like ready minions do.

An untapped vamp in torpor with two blood may rescue herself,
and if successful will be ready, tapped, and with zero blood.

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
Just my opinions. I would like to see the followings in
VAMPIRE (the Revised Jyhad):

1. Global Errata: release an official law that states that
all alpha cards are assumed to have revised wordings whenever
any player in the game demands it. I never liked the
distinction between the Revised Fog and the Unlimited Fog
in MtG. If you're changing the game for the better by
the revision, why not do it wholeheartedly? If you think
that the revised wordings make the /game/ better than
the possibly problematic alpha wording, why go
wishy-washy and let the alpha card effects remain
in the game (and possibly break it)?

2. Malkavian Dementia: maybe it's just me, but this
card makes me feel uncomfortable. Taking control of
a Vampire for one turn with a Master is normally okay,
but the card too easily allows for "unfair" combos.
There are many Jyhad cards which are very powerful,
but have serious drawbacks. However, if I play it
on a stolen Vampire, then my poor opponent suffer
/both/ the effects and the drawbacks. Jyhad is
not Magic, and should not have this kind of stuff, IMO.
Losing my 9-point Justicar to Bum's Rush+Wolf's Claws+Amaranth
is okay, because that's what those cards are supposed to do,
and there are many ways to prevent it; but losing
an old Malk. to Malk. Dementia+(take blood off Vampire
Master) is "unfair", IMO, because that other Master
is not "supposed" to be used to take blood off
opponent's Vampire, and this is virtually un-preventable
(except Sudden Reversal).

There should be things that even a crazy vampire would not
do! I'd suggest that the revised Malk. Dementia explicitly
states that, during the opponent's term of control:
1. no equipment can be taken from this Vampire (with the
normal "Take Equipment" action);
2. the term of control does not actually begin until
the end of the Master Phase, so the stealing player
cannot play a second Master card on him that specifically
targets friendly controlled Vampires;
3. certain actions/action modifiers are specifically
prohibited (EX: Day Operation)

Alan.

--

"Live Life with Heart."

Alan Kwan kw...@cs.cornell.edu
